text:
morgan: quick sync — noticed a sharp latency cliff on long prompts when running the new fused Flash + paged-attn path on canary. can we run a focused canary matrix (1/2/4 batch, seq 1024/2048/4096) and collect nvprof + kv-cache traces?

bench-bot: created canary job -> https://ci.redwood.local/bench/4821 :gear: running matrix (batch 1,2,4 x seq 1024/2048/4096) on gpnx-32g. artifacts will upload to /artifacts/4821/ (logs + perf).

samir: saw this locally too — 95th jumps around seq=2048 for fused opchain + paged prefetch. quick numbers from my run (batch=1): median 120ms, 95th 320ms at 1024; at 2048 median 150ms, 95th 760ms, tail 1.2s once KV eviction starts.

ciara: can you paste the exact command you ran? and did you enable async memcpy on the runtime? that changes overlap with prefetch.

samir: command I used:```bash
./bench_runner --model gpt-base-flash --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --paged-attn=true --fuse-opchain=true --async-mem=on
```

kevin: tagging perf note — when KV cache eviction happens we see a burst on memcpy and kernel rebinds. worth checking whether prefetch window size + async memcpy interacts poorly. also check cublas/cuDNN kernel versions.

morgan: bench-bot — can you add a variant with REDWOOD_PAGED_PREFETCH=0.1 and one with async-mem off? also capture memory maps and the pagefault counters if available.

bench-bot: added env variants to job 4821: PREFETCH=0.1, PREFETCH=0.5, ASYNC_MEM=off. artifacts will be in separate folders per variant.

ciara: if you can, collect the KV dump flag: set REDWOOD_KV_DUMP=1 to get eviction start/stop markers in logs. that'll help correlate memcpy spikes to eviction events.

samir: added that to my local runs. dump shows eviction kicks at token 1987 for seq=2048 run (batch=1). memory pressure oscillates thereafter. attaching quick excerpt:```text
[KV] eviction_start token=1987 free_before=1.2GB free_after=400MB
[memcpy] async submit t=1987 -> queued 12ms, start 48ms, done 260ms
```

morgan: perfect — that lines up. hypothesis: paged prefetch + fused kernels cause short-lived memory pressure peaks that defeat async overlap at the tail, producing the latency cliff. next steps: (1) run the canary variants (bench-bot) (2) try disabling prefetch or shrinking window (3) add a guard in scheduler to postpone fusion when free memory < X.

ciara: I can prepare a small PR to gate fusion behind a mem-check + heuristic flag REDWOOD_FUSE_GUARD=1. will push to draft and ping for review. PR will include unit test to simulate low free memory.

kevin: longshot: also try switching to contiguous kernel allocation (avoid small fragmented chunks). might reduce memcpy fragmentation. can add as an extra variant.

samir: one more datapoint — with async-mem off but PREFETCH=0.1 the 95th at 2048 drops to ~360ms. so reducing prefetch helps. full numbers in artifact.

morgan: great. can everyone add a one-line summary of their expectation for canary so we can pick the top 3 variants to run overnight? quick bullets: samir: reduce prefetch. ciara: fuse guard. kevin: contiguous alloc. morgan: baseline + async-mem toggle.

ciara: drafting PR now -> https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/639 (WIP). ping @samir for perf numbers to include in description.

bench-bot: canary job 4821 finished first pass. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.local/artifacts/4821/variants.tar.gz (logs, nvprof, kv-dumps). summary.csv included.

samir: grabbing artifacts now. will post a short summary in this thread when I finish parsing.

morgan: thanks all — if summary shows consistent repro we can schedule a short sync tomorrow 10am PT to decide mitigation path. otherwise async updates here are fine. :calendar:
